verdictReason: Killed. Outbound webhooks with retries, signing and a customer portal are already free and permissively licensed (Svix MIT, Hookdeck Outpost Apache-2.0, which also sells a managed tier from $10 per million events with SOC 2), and a DPA is a free CC BY 4.0 template, so a $29 flat bundle has no exclusive or compounding edge: any host or incumbent copies it by editing a price page. Pessimistic year 1 is -$281 cash on ~680 owner hours. Not verified: Svix/Hook Mesh/EventDock/Hook0 pricing pages (fetch blocked), whether any small vendor pays for a DPA plan.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: Several, all read on GitHub. Svix's own server is open source under MIT and self-hostable (D1). Hookdeck Outpost is Apache-2.0 'infrastructure for sending webhooks ... to your customers' systems' with retries, tenant isolation and an end-user portal, and Hookdeck sells a managed version with SOC 2 and 'usage-based pricing starting at $10 per million events' (D2), i.e. about $1 per 100k messages versus the entrant's $29. Convoy has a free community tier with a customer-facing webhook dashboard and signing (D3). Hook0 offers a free cloud tier with event-based pricing (D4). For one-stack teams, MIT libraries such as spatie/laravel-webhook-server give HMAC signing and exponential-backoff retries for free (D7). The Standard Webhooks spec removes design cost (D5). The 'DPA included' piece is not scarce: Common Paper publishes a DPA free to use and modify under CC BY 4.0 (D6). The case file (not re-verified, fetch blocked) also lists Svix Basic $20 with a 99.9% SLA (DEV-01-E1), Hook Mesh $39 (DEV-01-E5) and EventDock $29, i.e. near-identical flat plans already exist. Not confirmed: whether Outpost managed has a minimum fee or signs DPAs.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None identified. The wedge is a price point plus a bundled DPA. Both are copyable in days: the delivery code is MIT (Svix) or Apache-2.0 (Outpost), so any host can run the same stack (D1, D2); the DPA is a free template (D6); Svix could move its DPA to a lower tier or Hookdeck could cut its managed minimum without cost. There is no data network effect or lock-in in delivery, and the entrant's anonymity is a handicap for a processor of customers' payloads. Note Hook0 (SSPL, 'You may not provide the products to others as a managed service', D4) and Convoy (Elastic License v2, D3) cannot be resold as a managed service, so the entrant would have to use Svix/Outpost code or build its own. Falsifier that would reopen the idea: evidence that Svix, Hookdeck and the $29-59 flat-plan vendors all refuse DPAs below ~$490 AND that small vendors pay $29 to get one.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: Payment for hosted webhook infrastructure by larger buyers is plausible (Hookdeck sells a managed Outpost with SOC 2, SSO and RBAC at usage-based prices, D2; Svix pricing in the case file, DEV-01-E1, not re-verified). No page I could read shows a small API vendor paying $29/mo specifically for a DPA-included plan. The pain evidence in the case file (DEV-01-E2, E3, E4) is third-party blog/review complaints about the $490 step, and DEV-01-E2/E3 come from webhooker.eu, which itself appears to sell a competing product (not re-verified). Complaint is not payment.

answers.question: (4) Legal and platform constraints?
answers.answer: The entrant would be a GDPR Article 28 processor of its customers' webhook payloads (which can carry personal data), so it needs a DPA, a sub-processor list and breach duties; the template itself is free (D6) but being a credible processor as an anonymous solo operator is the hard part. Buyers may ask for SOC 2 (Hookdeck's managed Outpost already advertises it, D2); a SOC 2 audit is not budgeted here. Delivery to customer-supplied URLs creates SSRF and abuse risk (mitigation cost not sourced). Licence limits: Hook0 SSPL bars offering it as a managed service (D4); Convoy's ELv2 is generally understood to bar the same (general knowledge, not read on the page); Svix MIT and Outpost Apache-2.0 allow hosting, with Outpost logos/trademarks excluded (D1, D2). Depends on a cloud host and a payment processor.

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers?
answers.answer: Bottom-up (all inputs assumptions except where cited): price $29/mo; first revenue month 3 (reference entrant: day 70); 1.2 new payers per month with 3% monthly churn gives ~60 customer-months; revenue365 about $1,752. Costs: hosting/DB/queue $40/mo ($480), card fees 2.9% + $0.30 (~$69), one-off $145 (domain, terms/privacy generator, status/monitoring), total about $694; profit about $1,058 before owner time, about $1.6/hour over ~676 hours. Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5): revenue about $701, cost about $982, profit about -$281. Price pressure anchor: Outpost managed at $10 per million events (D2).

killReasons.reason: Free and cheap alternatives already cover the wedge: permissively licensed open-source senders with retries, signing and portals (Svix MIT, Outpost Apache-2.0), plus a managed Outpost from $10 per million events (about $1 per 100k messages) with SOC 2, versus a $29 flat price.

No structural edge: the wedge is a price plus a bundled DPA. The delivery code is MIT/Apache so any host can run the same stack, the DPA is a free CC BY 4.0 template, and an incumbent can add a DPA to a lower tier at no cost. Nothing is exclusive or compounding.

Pessimistic year-1 model is negative (about -$281 cash; base about $1.6 per owner hour over ~676 hours) because the price anchor is far below $29 for volume buyers and there is no demonstrated flow of small vendors paying for a DPA plan.

Hook0 (SSPL) bars offering it as a managed service and Convoy uses the Elastic License v2, narrowing which existing code the entrant can legally host; only MIT/Apache stacks (Svix, Outpost) are clean starting points.
Trust handicap: an anonymous solo operator is the processor of customers' payloads while Hookdeck's managed offering already advertises SOC 2; whether target buyers require SOC 2 is unverified.

assumptions: Assumption: price $29/month per customer (the case-file wedge price, not validated by any purchase).

Assumption: first revenue in month 3 (reference entrant: day 70); 1.2 new paying customers per month from month 3; 3% monthly churn; about 60 customer-months in year 1. No audience, so growth comes from search and developer communities; no source supports the rate.
Assumption: hosting, managed database and queue $40/month ($480/year); open-source Svix/Outpost code gives $0 licence cost (D1, D2).
Assumption: card fees 2.9% + $0.30 per charge (about $69/year); one-off costs $145 (domain, terms/privacy generator, status page/monitoring); DPA from the free Common Paper template, $0 (D6).
Excluded: SOC 2 audit, SSRF/abuse-mitigation engineering time, paid legal review, owner time (13 h/week, about 676 h, about $1.6/hour at base profit).
Pessimistic = price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5 applied to the base model: revenue about $701, cost about $982, profit about -$281.
Price anchor read: Outpost managed from $10 per million events (D2), so 100k messages is about $1.

legalNotes: GDPR Article 28: a webhook sender that relays customers' payloads is a processor and needs a DPA, sub-processor list and breach-notice terms (general knowledge, not read on a page); a free template exists (D6) but the credibility of an anonymous solo processor is the issue.
Delivering to customer-supplied URLs carries SSRF and abuse risk (internal-address blocking, rate limiting); engineering and liability cost not sourced.

Licences: Hook0 SSPL forbids offering it as a managed service (D4); Convoy is Elastic License v2 (D3; the managed-service restriction is general knowledge, not read on the page); Svix is MIT (D1); Outpost is Apache-2.0 with logos and trademarks excluded (D2).
Depends on a cloud host and a card processor; buyers may request an uptime SLA and SOC 2 (not verified).
